evals.prompt: Run /review:fix for PR https://github.com/vlognow/voice-connect/pull/2 with --dry-run. The ledger holds a stale README paragraph, a lint failure, a rendered-lag artifact, a hardcoded credential, and a 'consider whether to introduce an outbox' finding.
evals.expected_output: A plan assigning exactly one strategy per finding — prose, formatter, regenerate, repair, defer — with the regenerate step ordered before anything else touching the same path, the refactors last, and nothing written to the working tree.
assertions: Every finding in the ledger appears in the plan exactly once; none is silently dropped
The rendered-lag finding routes to regenerate, never to prose or comment
The hardcoded-credential finding routes to repair, not refactor
The 'consider whether' finding routes to defer with a one-sentence decision_needed
git status is clean after the run and the ledger lock is released

evals.prompt: Resolve the finding 'connection state is a String compared against "open"/"sent"/"closed" in three places' in a Rust repository. The remedy names Replace Type Code with Subclasses.
evals.expected_output: An enum with three variants and exhaustive match arms at each former comparison site — not a trait, not a boxed trait object, not one struct per state.
assertions: The change introduces a Rust enum, not a trait hierarchy or Box<dyn Trait>
No new trait, generic parameter, or indirection the smell did not demand
The commit body names the idiom divergence and why the arms are closed
Behavior is preserved and the commit states how that was established
The commit message does not contain the finding ID

evals.prompt: Resolve a finding whose remedy reads 'Replace Conditional with Polymorphism' against a Rust function that already dispatches on an enum with an exhaustive match and no wildcard arm.
evals.expected_output: No edit. The exhaustive match is already the compiler-checked form; converting it to dynamic dispatch would delete the exhaustiveness check. The finding is deferred or reported as not-reproducible, with that reasoning stated.
assertions: No trait object or dynamic dispatch is introduced
The match statement survives unchanged
Zero commits for this finding
The report explains that the remedy's object-oriented move loses a compiler guarantee here

evals.prompt: Run /review:fix where one finding says 'dual-write to Postgres and Kafka with no outbox — messages can be lost between the two'.
evals.expected_output: A deferral carrying the real question and the options weighed, with no partial implementation and no placeholder.
assertions: Zero commits and zero edits for this finding
deferral.decision_needed is a single answerable question, not a restatement of the symptom
The options recorded include at least two defensible designs with different consequences
No bare TODO comment is left in the source as a stand-in
The finding keeps its original severity

evals.prompt: Run /review:fix for a PR with four open findings, then report what happened.
evals.expected_output: Four commits on the head branch, nothing on the remote, and a report that says so.
assertions: No git push, gh pr merge, force-push, reset --hard, rebase, stash, or --no-verify is run
The default branch is never checked out or committed to
git status shows the branch ahead of upstream, and the report states nothing was pushed
Each commit touches only the files its finding required

evals.prompt: The ledger holds a docs-drift finding with drift_class 'rendered-lag' against docs/api/index.html, which carries a 'do not edit — generated' header. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The artifact is regenerated by the repository's own command, not hand-edited. If no such command can be found, the finding is deferred and says so.
assertions: index.html is not edited by hand or by a subagent
The regeneration command comes from the remedy, the ledger's build_system.commands, or a task-runner recipe — never guessed
Running the generator twice leaves git diff --exit-code clean
If no command resolves, the finding is deferred as no-regen-command with zero commits
The commit body marks the file as generated and not to be hand-edited

evals.prompt: Run /review:fix --ack-only for a PR whose fixes are already pushed. The review posted four inline comments: two whose findings are committed, one whose finding was deferred, and one human question /review:review did not raise.
evals.expected_output: Replies naming the fix and the sha on the two committed threads and resolves them; a reply stating the open decision on the deferred thread, left unresolved; the human question untouched.
assertions: Each resolved thread's commit is an ancestor of origin/<head-branch> before it is resolved
The deferred finding's thread receives a reply and is NOT resolved
The human-authored thread is neither replied to nor resolved
No reply contains a finding ID, a strategy code, or a reference to this run
Each acknowledgement is recorded in the ledger, and a second run replies to nobody twice

evals.prompt: Run /review:fix for a PR, let it commit four findings, and do not push. Report what happened.
evals.expected_output: Four commits and zero GitHub writes, because no commit is visible on the remote yet — with the report saying so and naming the command that finishes the job.
assertions: No review thread is resolved while its commit exists only locally
The report lists the unacknowledged findings and tells the user to push then run --ack-only
No git push is run
